prompt.text:
Implement a checked integer expression evaluator in `solution.rs` using only the standard library.

Expose this exact API:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EvalError {
    EmptyExpression,
    UnexpectedToken(usize),
    MissingClosingParen,
    DivisionByZero,
    Overflow,
}

pub fn evaluate(source: &str) -> Result<i64, EvalError>;
```

Support decimal nonnegative integer literals, parentheses, unary `+` and `-`, and binary `+`, `-`, `*`, and `/`. Multiplication and division bind more tightly than addition and subtraction; binary operators associate left-to-right. Unary operators may be chained. ASCII whitespace may occur between tokens. Any other character is invalid, and `UnexpectedToken` contains its byte offset.

Use checked `i64` arithmetic, including literal parsing, negation, and the `i64::MIN / -1` case. Division truncates toward zero. Report `DivisionByZero` when appropriate. An empty or whitespace-only input returns `EmptyExpression`. An opening parenthesis without a matching closing parenthesis returns `MissingClosingParen`. Extra tokens, empty parentheses, missing operands, and unmatched closing parentheses return `UnexpectedToken` at the first offending byte; when an operand is missing at end-of-input, use `source.len()`. The input must not be mutated.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
